s: A company has developed a mobile game. The backend for the game runs on several virtual machines located in an on-premises data center. The business logic is exposed using a REST API with multiple functions. Player session data is stored in central file storage. Backend services use different API keys for throttling and to distinguish between live and test traffic. The load on the game backend varies throughout the day. During peak hours, the server capacity is not sufficient. There are also latency issues when fetching player session data. Management has asked a solutions architect to present a cloud architecture that can handle the game's varying load and provide low-latency data access. The API model should not be changed. Which solution meets these requirements?
o: Implement the REST API using a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Run the business logic on an Amazon EC2 instance behind the NLB. Store player session data in Amazon Aurora Serverless.
Implement the REST API using an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Run the business logic in AWS Lambda. Store player session data in Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity.
Implement the REST API using Amazon API Gateway. Run the business logic in AWS Lambda. Store player session data in Amazon DynamoDB with on- demand capacity.
Implement the REST API using AWS AppSync. Run the business logic in AWS Lambda. Store player session data in Amazon Aurora Serverless.

w.y: The REST API model must stay the same and API keys are used for throttling and for separating live and test traffic. Amazon API Gateway supports this natively with REST APIs, API keys and usage plans. Lambda scales automatically with the varying load, and DynamoDB on-demand gives single-digit-millisecond access to session data without capacity planning.

o.A: A single EC2 instance doesn't scale with the load, and an NLB has no concept of API keys or usage-plan throttling.
o.B: ALBs can invoke Lambda but don't support API keys or usage plans, so the throttling and key model is lost.
o.C: Correct: API Gateway keeps the REST model with API keys and usage plans, Lambda scales, and DynamoDB gives low-latency session data.
o.D: AppSync is GraphQL, which changes the API model, and Aurora Serverless is slower than DynamoDB for key-value session lookups.

s: Usage plans and API keys for REST APIs in API Gateway
